name: squad-ux-communication
description: "Use UX communication to explain the user problem, design decision, trade-offs, expected impact, and implementation intent clearly to accountable collaborators."
---

# Communication Skills

## Procedure
1. Identify the authorized decision, audience, evidence, and accountable owners. Store communication artifacts only in approved product locations.
2. Explain the problem, proposed solution, and expected impact in plain language. Distinguish observed outcomes from hypotheses and illustrate actual task states.
3. Include rationale, alternatives, constraints, acceptance criteria, risks, and the precise decision requested. Do not hide limitations behind visual polish or jargon.
4. Ask receiving collaborators to confirm interpretation and responsibilities. Record disagreement and missing evidence rather than inventing agreement.
5. Return a decision/implementation handoff with owner, artifacts, next action, and validation criteria. ProductOwner retains priority and Kanban owns card changes.

## Completion Checks
The receiver can identify intended behavior and the required decision. A presentation is not approval, comprehension evidence, or completed delivery by itself.

## Source
Original procedure informed by item 7 of [UX Playbook's UX skills article](https://uxplaybook.org/articles/top-skills-every-ux-designer-needs), accessed October 11, 2026.
